_comment: The swap table. TWO mechanisms: (1) `groups` = sets of interchangeable ingredients, any member can stand in for any other. (2) `rules` = one-directional swaps (`from` -> one of `to`). The app uses this to mark a recipe cookable even when you are missing an ingredient, and to rewrite the ingredient line with what you actually have.
_functions: A recipe ingredient can declare `function` (e.g. sweetness, binding, bulk, browning, fat, acid, richness). A swap is CLEAN when the stand-in provides every function the recipe needs, and FLAGGED (with a `compensate` tip) when it does not. That is what stops the app from telling you to bind a granola bar with 8 drops of stevia.

groups.name: Sweeteners
groups.note: Liquid sweeteners are interchangeable by volume. Zero-calorie ones give sweetness only, so watch out for recipes where the syrup was also doing the sticking, the bulk or the browning.

members.amount: 2 medjool dates, blended with 1 tsp warm water
members.notes: Blend into a paste first, or soak 10 min if dry.
Melt with a splash of warm water for liquid recipes.
Honey is sweeter than sugar, so you need slightly more sugar. Add 1 tsp extra liquid to the recipe.

members.amount: 6-8 drops liquid, or a scant 1/4 tsp powder
members.compensate: Replace the missing volume: for each tbsp of syrup swapped out, add ~1 tbsp of the recipe's own liquid (milk/water) for batters, or ~1 tbsp extra nut butter / date paste where the syrup was holding things together.
members.notes: Taste as you go - brands vary a lot in strength, and too much reads bitter.

members.amount: 8-10 drops liquid, or 1 tbsp + 1 tsp granulated
members.compensate: Granulated monk fruit keeps the bulk, so only liquid drops need a volume top-up. Nothing replaces the stickiness - add nut butter or date paste if the recipe relied on it.
members.notes: Cleanest tasting of the zero-calorie options; blends usually measure 1:1 against sugar.

members.compensate: Keeps volume but will not caramelise. Erythritol also has a cooling aftertaste and can recrystallise when cold - allulose behaves better in anything chilled or chewy.
members.notes: About 70% as sweet as sugar, so use a bit more.

groups.name: Cooking fats
groups.note: Swap by volume. The differences are smoke point and flavour, not chemistry.

members.notes: Fine up to a medium sear; too fruity for most Indian tempering.

members.compensate: Butter burns above a medium flame - drop the heat, or use half butter half oil.

members.notes: Virgin coconut oil tastes strongly of coconut; refined does not.
Heat to smoking then cool slightly to take the raw edge off.

members.compensate: Great for air fryer and non-stick, useless anywhere the fat is part of the sauce.

groups.name: Finishing acids
groups.note: Anything sour that brightens a finished dish.

members.notes: Sharper than lemon, so start with less. Apple cider and rice vinegar are the gentlest; balsamic brings its own sweetness and colour.

members.compensate: Stir in off the heat so it does not split.

groups.name: Thick, creamy dairy
groups.note: For dips, marinades, dressings and bowls. All of these are the high-protein, low-fat way to get creaminess.

members.amount: 3/4 cup, strained 20 min in a cloth
members.compensate: Regular curd is much looser. Strain it, or accept a thinner sauce.
Blend it or it stays lumpy. Add a squeeze of lemon for the tang.
Dairy-free route. Add lemon or vinegar for the sourness.
members.notes: Silken tofu only - firm tofu will not blend smooth.

members.compensate: Adds coconut flavour and a lot of fat - fine in curries, odd in a raita.

groups.name: Milks
groups.note: Interchangeable 1:1 in anything poured, soaked or blended.

members.compensate: Roughly 1g protein per cup vs 8g in dairy. If protein is the point of the recipe, add a scoop of whey or use soy milk.

members.notes: The only plant milk with protein close to dairy.

members.compensate: Last resort. Works in oats and smoothies; makes anything creamy taste thin.

groups.name: Egg (as a binder)
groups.note: Only for eggs that are holding something together - pancakes, tikkis, muffins, meatballs. Nothing here replaces eggs in an omelette or scramble. Everything in here is safe in a savoury recipe; the sweet-only stand-ins live in egg_binder_sweet, so pin a savoury line to this group to keep them out.

members.amount: 1 tbsp ground + 3 tbsp water, rested 5 min
members.compensate: The classic flax egg. Holds things together but will not make anything rise - fine for tikkis and cookies, weak in cakes.
Same idea as a flax egg. Leaves visible specks.
The Indian answer - what holds a tikki together. Cook it through or it tastes raw.

groups.name: Egg (as a binder, sweet bakes only)
groups.note: Sweet recipes only. Mashed banana binds as well as an egg but brings its own flavour and sugar, which is fine in oats or cookies and wrong in anything savoury. A line left unpinned searches this group too, so pin savoury lines to egg_binder.

members.compensate: Brings sweetness and banana flavour - dial back the other sweeteners. Never in a savoury recipe.

groups.name: Firm plant proteins
groups.note: Cube-shaped protein that holds its shape in a pan. Cooking times are close enough to swap directly.

members.compensate: Press out the water or it will not brown. Salt it earlier than you would paneer - it is blander.

members.notes: Steam 10 min first to take out the bitterness.

members.amount: 50 g dry, soaked in hot salted water 15 min and squeezed
members.compensate: Squeeze them properly dry - waterlogged chunks will not take up any masala.
members.notes: Cheapest protein in this list by a distance.

groups.name: Blendable creamy bases
groups.note: Soft protein that blends to a smooth cream for desserts and thick drinks. Not the same list as the firm cube-shaped proteins - anything that stays grainy in a blender does not belong here.

members.notes: Blend it longer than feels necessary. Fresh paneer goes smoother than shop-bought.

members.amount: 200 g silken, or firm blended a little longer
members.compensate: Blander and less rich than paneer. Taste before chilling and add a little more sweetener.
Looser, and it sets softer. Fine where melted chocolate is doing the setting; it will not hold a piped shape on its own.
Blend it properly or it stays lumpy.

groups.name: Lean meat and fish
groups.note: Swappable in most marinated / pan-cooked / air-fried recipes. Adjust the cook time.

members.notes: Dries out fast - pull it the moment it is done.
More forgiving, a few minutes longer, slightly more fat.

members.compensate: Cooks in roughly half the time and will fall apart if you stir it. Add it late.
3-4 minutes total, no more.
Vegetarian route. Needs no cooking through, just browning - add it at the end.
Vegetarian route. Soak, squeeze, then treat like the meat.

groups.name: Grain bases
groups.note: The thing under the curry / in the bowl. Cooked volumes swap 1:1; uncooked quantities and water ratios do not.

members.notes: Roughly double the cooking time of white rice.
Rinse it first or it tastes soapy. 1:2 with water, 15 min.
Fastest option - just pour over boiling water and cover for 5 min.

members.compensate: Low-carb route. Cook it dry in a hot pan first or the bowl turns watery.

groups.name: Leafy greens
groups.note: Wilting greens are interchangeable; the sturdier ones need longer.

members.notes: Wilts in about a minute.

members.compensate: Needs 3-4 minutes and a pinch of salt to soften.

members.notes: Distinctly bitter - great in Indian dishes, wrong in a Caesar.

members.compensate: Firmer and sweeter; give it 5 minutes.
Raw only - it collapses to nothing when cooked.

members.notes: Bitter and savoury rather than sweet - better in dressings than in desserts.

members.amount: 1/4 cup soaked and blended with 1 tbsp water

members.compensate: Sweeter and much less salty - use more, and add a pinch of salt. Soy-free and gluten-free.
Dry, so it will not deglaze a pan.

groups.name: Flours
groups.note: Only partly interchangeable - the gluten-free ones behave very differently. Swap up to half the flour and you will usually be fine.

members.compensate: No gluten, so batters spread more and breads will not rise the same. Blitz rolled oats to make it yourself.
members.notes: Best for pancakes, muffins and cookies.

members.compensate: Very low carb but no binding at all - needs an extra egg, and everything comes out denser and more fragile.
Tastes distinctly of gram - great in savoury batters, wrong in a cake. Must be cooked through.
Heavy and earthy - blend half-and-half with wheat flour for rotis that still fold.

members.amount: 1 cup chopped, whites and greens split
members.compensate: Cooks in a minute instead of ten and never goes brown and jammy.

groups.name: Soft fresh herbs
groups.note: Swappable in quantity, but each one changes the dish's identity. Use as a garnish-level swap.

members.notes: The go-to if coriander tastes of soap to you.

members.compensate: Much stronger - use about half.

members.notes: Add off the heat.

members.compensate: Assertive and aniseedy - use about half.
Brings vinegar with it - fine in a marinade, sharp in a dal.
Dairy-free stand-in for the savoury hit only - it will never melt or brown.

members.notes: More consistent than sad winter tomatoes.

members.compensate: Concentrated - dilute it, and fry the paste for a minute first.

members.notes: Nut-free option.
Nut-free option.

members.compensate: Much smaller - use about half by volume.

groups.name: Quick-cooking dals
groups.note: Swap freely; adjust water and time.

members.notes: Fastest - 20 min in a pan, breaks down completely.
Lightest and easiest to digest.

members.compensate: Needs a pressure cooker or 45 min of simmering.
Soak 30 min first and pressure cook - it holds its shape rather than melting.
About half the protein and a lot more volume - the smoothie gets thicker and tangier.
Only ~8 g of protein and 190 calories - not really a like-for-like swap.

members.notes: Dairy-free, and tasteless in a smoothie.

to.amount: 1 cup + 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar, rested 5 min

rules.note: Chaas / lassi base. The acid is the point.

to.notes: Higher protein, lower fat, basically identical in a dip.

to.amount: 1:1 + 1/2 tsp mustard + a squeeze of lemon
to.notes: Saves ~80 calories per tablespoon and adds protein.
Off the heat only, or it splits.

to.amount: 1/4 cup soaked, blended with 1/4 cup water

to.notes: Low-carb; browns faster, so drop the heat.

to.amount: same volume + 1/4 tsp salt per cup

to.notes: Lower smoke point - keep the flame down.
Not the same flavour, but it fills the herbal gap. Honestly, the dish is fine without it.

to.amount: 3/4 tsp + 1 tsp lemon juice, added right before steaming
to.notes: Mix and get it in the steamer immediately.

to.amount: 1/4 tsp + 1/2 tsp lemon juice or vinegar per 1 tsp baking powder
1 litre full-fat + 2 tbsp lemon juice, curdled and hung 30 min = ~200 g paneer
1/2 tsp dried ginger powder per 1 tbsp fresh

to.notes: Low-carb; will not hold a heavy sauce.
Different but excellent, especially in anything milk-based.
